title: Join + consent hard-gate + fail-closed bot resolution
intent: Proxy joins from a meeting link (or calendar invite) as a Recall bot with no host-side install, and its FIRST observable action is the one-line consent notice — a hard gate, not a courtesy (spec §3.1). The gate means nothing is observed/recorded/routed until the notice posts: the JoinSession FSM opens LISTENING only after post_chat succeeds, and JoinSession.can_observe() is the predicate the HearingStage consent gate reads. The bot belongs to the room (no inviter-identity gate); every webhook bot_id resolves fail-closed to one meeting/tenant/repo (isolation triad at the transport boundary).
definition_of_done: Done = a real Recall bot launches from a link alone, writes recall_bot_id back to the meetings row, posts+pins the consent line as the first action, transitions to LISTENING within 10s, re-posts on late-join, defers to organizer on objection, ends on hard-removal, and reports join/post failure honestly (never a false joined/posted). Crucially, the harness must WIRE JoinSession.can_observe into HearingStage(can_observe=...) so pre-consent records are dropped (records_before_consent_allowed=0). NOT done if HearingStage is constructed with can_observe=None (defaults to always-allow) anywhere on the live join path — that silently bypasses the gate. For the [latency] criteria: the p95 latency SLO is proven on REAL Recall/Cartesia/Output-Media timing (a pinned real-data measurement), not sim — the offline test proves only the boundary-gated/canned shape.
integration_point: services/transport/src/transport/join.py (JoinSession) wired into meeting_runtime harness startup; JoinSession.can_observe injected into transport/hearing.py HearingStage(can_observe=...) at wire-up
acceptance: WHEN a meeting link (or calendar invite) is handed to the harness THE SYSTEM SHALL launch a Recall bot with no host install, post+pin the consent notice as the first observable action, and open observation only after the notice posts, within 10s.
invariants: Law 3 human control absolute — consent is a hard precondition gate, not a courtesy
Law 2 never overstate — join/post failure reported plainly, never a false joined/posted
Naming law — consent notice carries no internal component name; product+agent are Proxy (lint.naming)
Isolation triad — unknown bot_id fails closed, no cross-tenant default resolution
risks: FIX FOCUS: HearingStage._can_observe defaults to always-allow when can_observe=None (transport/hearing.py:130-131). Confirm the harness injects JoinSession.can_observe on the live join path — an un-wired gate silently permits pre-consent observation and violates AC-JOIN-04 (P0, F-RECORD-BEFORE-CONSENT). Verify by tracing the meeting_runtime wire-up, not just the unit test.

AC-JOIN-15 is [eval-realrepo] P1 — 'bot appears in a real Meet and consent line is really posted/pinned' needs a REAL Recall join, not the fake TransportProvider; the offline test proves the FSM shape only.
AC-JOIN-02 join-to-listening <=10s is a real-clock threshold — the sim asserts the boundary; the live wall-clock is a pinned M11 measurement.

title: Recall webhooks → roster / meeting-end / bot-status signals (durable-first)
intent: The transport streams live participant events (present-snapshot + join/leave deltas with names), meeting metadata (title+participants as init context, off the nine-signal surface), bot-status, and an EXPLICIT meeting-end — never inferred from silence (spec §3.1). Each webhook lands durably first (idempotent INSERT ON CONFLICT on delivery_guid in substrate.webhook_events), returns 200, and processes exactly once so a duplicate guid is a no-op; every emitted signal traces to a source-payload field, never synthesized. Meeting-end fires exactly once and triggers the close sequence AFTER the signal.
definition_of_done: Done = roster present/join/leave stream live (not batched) with resolved names, metadata delivered once as Orchestrator context, bot-status routed after durable persist, meeting-end emitted only on the explicit webhook (or terminal bot-removal) exactly once and BEFORE the close sequence, and every duplicate delivery_guid a proven no-op. The transport signal surface stays disjoint from the client ProxyMessage registry (assert_registry_closed passes without it). NOT done if any signal is synthesized rather than derived from a payload field, or meeting-end is inferred from silence.
integration_point: services/transport/src/transport/events.py (WebhookProcessor) drained by the meeting_runtime harness webhook endpoint over libs/db webhook_events
acceptance: WHEN a Recall participant/bot-status/meeting-end webhook is delivered THE SYSTEM SHALL persist it durably by delivery_guid, emit the corresponding roster/bot-status/meeting-end signal derived from the payload exactly once, and emit meeting-end only on the explicit event.
invariants: Law 1 grounded — every emitted signal traces to a source-payload field, never synthesized
Law 2 never overstate — meeting-end is explicit, never inferred from silence
Registry disjointness — roster/bot-status/meeting-end are internal over-transport events, out of assert_registry_closed scope (CANONICAL §11.8)
Exactly-once — delivery_guid dedupe; one MeetingEnd per close
risks: Real Recall teardown sends a SEQUENCE of terminal signals (bot-status call_ended/done + meeting.end/bot.removed), each a distinct delivery_guid the dedupe cannot collapse — the _ended guard must hold so close runs once (AC-EVENTS-06).
Metadata title+roster may ride SEPARATE payloads; the accumulate-both-before-deliver path (AC-EVENTS-05) needs a real split-payload case, not just a single combined fixture.
Confirm-at-build: the Recall webhook event tags/payload shape are pinned assumptions (CANONICAL §11.10 confirm-against-live-docs) — drift breaks derivation silently.

title: Hearing: per-speaker audio → speaker-attributed transcript fan-out (BYOK passthrough)
intent: Recall delivers per-speaker audio; STT is AssemblyAI Universal-Streaming via Recall's BYOK passthrough, so NO Proxy-side STT client is instantiated — transport only consumes the transcript passthrough (spec §3.2). One transcript stream fans over ONE in-process carrier to both Doc 03 (Notes) and Doc 04 (Orchestrator) with identical ordered records keeping speaker + timestamps. Proxy's own speech is present labelled 'Proxy' but is inert — never routed as an ask (it must not respond to itself). The wire parser is fail-loud: drift raises rather than parsing on a silent assumption. Buffer-through-a-hiccup is NOT ours under BYOK; the honest fallback is the mark-lost gap path.
definition_of_done: Done = a two-speaker stream yields correctly attributed live transcript records, both consumers receive the identical ordered sequence, Proxy-labelled lines are recorded but zero are routed as asks, every human line IS routed, malformed passthrough raises loudly, and un-transcribed stretches surface as explicit mark-lost gaps. NOT done if any Proxy-side STT SDK/client is instantiated, if a buffer-through-outage handler is added (that over-promises resilience we don't own), or if attribution/latency is only proven in sim.
integration_point: services/transport/src/transport/hearing.py (HearingStage.ingest_wire_transcript) fanning onto the SignalCarrier the Doc 03 notes engine subscribes to (DOC02-DOC03-TRANSCRIPT-BRIDGE)
acceptance: WHEN Recall passthrough delivers per-speaker transcript messages THE SYSTEM SHALL emit one speaker-attributed record per message onto the shared carrier for both Doc 03 and Doc 04, route only non-Proxy lines as asks, and mark any un-transcribed stretch lost — instantiating no Proxy-side STT client.
invariants: Law 1 grounded — un-transcribed audio marked lost, never silently absent
CANONICAL §10.3 — a Proxy-labelled transcript line is untrusted inert data, never an instruction
No Proxy-side STT client under BYOK (AC-HEAR-02); zero silent wire assumptions (fail-loud parser)
One in-process carrier fan-out — no bus/broker/wire between transport and its consumers
risks: AC-HEAR-05 word-latency ~300ms p50 is [latency] P1 — needs REAL Recall→AssemblyAI timing, not sim; the offline test asserts the emit_t-spoken_t measurement shape only, not the live number.
AC-HEAR-06 two-speaker attribution correctness is [eval-realrepo] P1 — needs real code-heavy engineering audio scored against a golden, not a synthetic fixture.

AC-HEAR-10 code-heavy accuracy vs one alternative is [eval-realrepo] P1 — the pinned side-by-side engine test must run on real identifiers/filenames/acronyms before locking the engine; NOT provable in sim.
Confirm-at-build: Recall real-time transcript passthrough + AAI turn payload wire shape is pinned (wire.py provenance) — reconfirm against live vendor docs.

title: Turn-taking: Silero-VAD barge-in + AAI end_of_turn boundary + hard-mute
intent: Two clean, deterministic signals stream continuously (spec §3.6): speaking(on/off) from Silero VAD (<1ms/chunk, CPU) — the sub-200ms barge-in trigger, sourced from VAD never the ~300ms AAI transcript; and boundary(now) from AssemblyAI's end_of_turn on the paid STT stream — no Smart Turn v3 in V0 core, no timer/elapsed-silence boundary. Voice may start ONLY on a clear boundary; a mid-thought breath is not a boundary. Any human speech onset during Proxy's speech stops in-flight TTS mid-word then flushes the queue atomically; the small-chunk Output-Media buffer keeps a large buffer from defeating the cut. Barge-in never fires on Proxy's own audio or on silence. Hard-mute kills in-flight TTS and enters silent mode (voice off; tile+chat stay live) until re-invited — speaking and muted are mutually exclusive. The confirm-at-build boundary-source contingency wires Smart Turn v3 as fallback if Recall does not forward end_of_turn.
definition_of_done: Done = the surface is exactly the three signals {speaking,boundary,barge-in}, barge-in is VAD-sourced and stops TTS mid-word within budget + flushes the queue, boundary opens only on a real AAI end_of_turn (never a timer), barge-in never fires on Proxy/silence, hard-mute silences voice while tile+chat stay live and only a re-invite lifts it (speaking XOR muted), and the boundary source is resolved by a build probe (never unresolved). NOT done if barge-in is sourced from the transcript, a timer synthesizes a boundary, or the small-chunk buffer lets a large buffered stretch defeat the cut.
integration_point: services/transport/src/transport/turn.py (TurnController / TurnSignalPump) driven by VAD frames + STT messages; boundary source resolved in transport/boundary.py at harness startup
acceptance: WHEN a human speech onset occurs during Proxy's speech THE SYSTEM SHALL stop TTS mid-word within 200ms and flush the queue; WHEN an AAI end_of_turn arrives THE SYSTEM SHALL open a boundary and release the next queued utterance; WHEN 'Proxy, quiet' is invoked THE SYSTEM SHALL silence voice while keeping tile+chat live until re-invited.
invariants: Law 3 human control — barge-in stops speech mid-word; hard-mute is a human kill-switch
Law 4 dynamic — recognition of 'quiet' is Doc 04's; the kill-switch mechanism is here
Barge-in sourced from Silero VAD only, never the AAI transcript (AC-TURN-01)
No Smart Turn v3 / no timer boundary in V0 core (CANONICAL §12.11); boundary is AAI end_of_turn or the probed fallback
risks: AC-TURN-09 barge-in stop <200ms and AC-TURN-15 are effectively-instant latency claims — the real mid-word cut budget needs live VAD→abort→Output-Media-flush timing, not sim (the M4 mechanism runs against fakes).

CONFIRM-AT-BUILD (§3.9-7): verify Recall passthrough actually forwards AAI's end_of_turn field. If it does NOT, the boundary probe must wire Smart Turn v3 as a REAL fallback boundary source (AC-TURN-16, F-NO-BOUNDARY-FALLBACK) — not merely record the decision.
The small-chunk buffer (tts_chunk_ms/max_buffered_audio_ms < barge_in_budget_ms) must actually bound residual playout so a barge-in isn't defeated by buffered Output-Media audio (AC-TURN-10).

title: Speaking: text → one calm voice + verbatim chat copy, headlines-only envelope
intent: Upstream hands text; this layer posts the verbatim chat copy FIRST (free — we have the text pre-synthesis — and it survives an audio-leg fault), then synthesizes the EXACT text with Cartesia Sonic 3 through the boundary-gated turn-core so voice begins only on a boundary and aborts instantly on barge-in (spec §3.3). Headlines-only is enforced here: a line over the soft cap or breaching the ~2-4k chars/hr budget is detail — routed to chat, never spoken, never substituted. One calm voice/register across every line. The ack-audible reflex fires a fixed canned <=500ms 'on it' line, distinct from the resolved answer, boundary-gated + barge-able on the same path; it degrades to the tile ACK when the hard char/hr ceiling would be breached.
definition_of_done: Done = the exact supplied text is synthesized (no headline auto-extraction/substitution), every spoken line has a byte-equal chat copy posted first, detail is routed to chat and never spoken, speaking begins only on a boundary and stops mid-word on barge-in, one voice identity across the run, and the canned ack is fixed+independent of the answer. NOT done if the ack content leaks the answer, a spoken line lacks its chat copy, or the char/hr envelope is not actually enforced against the summed synthesized total. For the [latency] criteria: the p95 latency SLO is proven on REAL Recall/Cartesia/Output-Media timing (a pinned real-data measurement), not sim — the offline test proves only the boundary-gated/canned shape.
integration_point: services/transport/src/transport/speak.py (SpeakOrchestrator) composing transport/turn.py TurnController; post_copy wired to the chat broadcast channel by the harness
acceptance: WHEN Doc 04 hands a line to speak THE SYSTEM SHALL post its verbatim chat copy first, synthesize the exact text in one calm voice only on a boundary within the headlines-only char/hr envelope, and abort mid-word on barge-in — routing over-budget/over-cap lines to chat instead of speaking.
invariants: Law 2 never overstate — every spoken line also posts verbatim as text (parity, accessibility+record)
Law 3 human control — speech aborts instantly on barge-in
Naming law — canned ack/spoken lines carry no internal name (lint.naming)
call_external seam — Cartesia synth issued only through libs.http.call_external; no raw client here
risks: AC-SPEAK-09 audible-ack p95<=500ms is [latency] P0 — the ack reflex latency needs real Cartesia TTFA (~40ms) + Output-Media timing, not sim; the offline test proves the fixed-canned/boundary-gated shape only.
AC-SPEAK-13 first-grounded-audio p50<=2.5s/p95<=5s is [latency] P0 (§12.8 SLO, shallow direct-answer path) — a real-data pinned M11 measurement, not a unit assertion.
The char/hr budget (4000) with the ack reserve is enforced against summed synthesize calls — verify the ack degrade-to-tile branch actually triggers under a real over-budget stream (AC-SPEAK-20).

title: Chat: inbound @proxy asks + outbound broadcast/DM + per-meeting channel report
intent: Chat is a first-class socket, not a lesser sibling of voice (spec §3.4). Inbound, every platform chat line arrives ONLY via the Recall seam and re-emits as a chat(message,sender,dm?) signal; an addressed line (@proxy token OR Doc 04's injected recognizer) forwards to the ask_sink as an ask IDENTICAL in shape to a spoken ask — differing solely in its recorded socket field. Outbound is pure plumbing: broadcast (detail/links/receipts/spoken-copy) exactly once verbatim; DM to EXACTLY one recipient where the platform supports it, never leaking to broadcast; channel-report reads dm_available from the REAL platform capability, never a constant. On a broadcast-only platform a DM mechanically degrades — handed to the upstream broadcast-or-hold hook, dropping nothing.
definition_of_done: Done = inbound lines stream only via Recall and always signal, addressed lines forward as socket-tagged asks shape-equal to spoken asks, non-addressed lines signal but never enter the ask path, broadcast posts once verbatim, DM lands to one recipient (never broadcast) or mechanically degrades to the upstream hook without dropping, and dm_available derives from the real seam (both branches reachable). NOT done if a chat ask is tagged a lesser class, a DM body leaks to broadcast, or dm_available is hard-coded. chat/channel-report stay out of the client registry.
integration_point: services/transport/src/transport/chat.py (ChatChannel) wired to Doc 04 ask_sink + Doc 04/06 degrade_hook by the harness; broadcast seam feeds SpeakOrchestrator.post_copy
acceptance: WHEN a chat line arrives via Recall THE SYSTEM SHALL emit a chat signal and, if addressed, forward it as a socket-tagged ask shape-equal to a spoken ask; WHEN Doc 04 sends outbound THE SYSTEM SHALL broadcast verbatim once or DM one recipient where dm_available (real capability), else degrade to the upstream hook without dropping.
invariants: Law 4 dynamic — this layer reports which channels exist; the broadcast-vs-hold judgment lives in Docs 04/06, injected
Registry disjointness — chat + channel-report are internal 02->03/04 events, never client ProxyMessage types (AC-CHAT-14)
call_external seam — all chat round-trips via the injected TransportProvider behind call_external; no raw client
Contracts reuse — ChannelReport imported from libs/contracts, never re-defined
risks: dm_available must derive from the REAL per-meeting platform capability with BOTH branches reachable — a broadcast-only platform (e.g. some Teams/Meet configs) is a real path, not a constant true (AC-CHAT-12/13).
The @proxy token is one accept path but not the only one — Doc 04's non-token 'any addressed form' recognizer must be injected, else un-prefixed addressed lines are dropped (AC-CHAT-16).
Confirm-at-build: Recall chat-in/chat-out + DM payload support is platform-dependent and a pinned assumption — reconfirm against live docs.

title: Canvas: one tile webpage + screenshare promote/demote, drawn social signals
intent: ONE canvas webpage per meeting, streamed by Recall Output Media as the ambient camera tile and promoted onto the shared screen at higher resolution for a STRUCTURED live-work progress view (spec §3.5). This layer owns the surface + stream + promote/demote mechanism ONLY — what frames LOOK like is Doc 08. All social signals (listening/checking/has-something/raise-hand/reaction) are drawn on canvas — no native platform-button call exists anywhere. The 'checking…' tile ACK is a drawn state within a <=500ms budget gated on a REAL in-flight LSP-bound resolve, never speculative. Camera and screen are mutually exclusive (one Surface enum); every swap is announced and upstream-triggered — the layer never self-promotes; the tile is outbound-only (no screen-ingestion).
definition_of_done: Done = exactly one page per meeting (duplicate refused), non-empty tile frames stream while active, social signals are drawn (no native-button path), the tile ACK draws only on a real in-flight resolve within budget, screenshare promotes the same page at higher res with the structured (not raw-pixel-mirror) view, swaps are mutually exclusive + announced + upstream-triggered, a promote/demote cycle drops neither stream (no black frame), the render WS authenticates via a meeting-scoped bearer never logged, and no inbound/ingest path exists. NOT done if a native raise-hand/reaction button is called, a swap self-initiates, or a raw-pixel/cursor mirror renderer appears.
integration_point: services/transport/src/transport/canvas.py (CanvasSurface / CanvasRegistry) streaming via the OutputMediaSink; Doc 08 renders the frame descriptors into pixels
acceptance: WHEN the harness opens a meeting THE SYSTEM SHALL stream exactly one canvas page as the camera tile with drawn (never native-button) social signals; WHEN an upstream trigger requests a promote THE SYSTEM SHALL swap the same page to the shared screen (mutually exclusive, announced) and demote back, dropping neither stream.
invariants: Law 3 human control — a promote is impossible without an upstream SwapTrigger; the layer never self-initiates
Law 4 dynamic — the layer executes the mechanism; the swap decision + frame appearance live in Docs 04/08
Screen-ingestion deferred — the tile is outbound-only; no read/ingest path (AC-CANVAS-12)
Secrets — the tile render WS bearer comes from Secret Manager (injected), never hard-coded or logged (AC-CANVAS-13)
Delivery authority — the projector is pure rendering and never speaks; the headline is spoken by the SPEAK verb (AC-XCUT-04)
risks: AC-CANVAS-15 frame-rate/smoothness is a pinned M11 MEASUREMENT (Recall publishes no number) — this file builds the functional shape (frames stream, stay live) and asserts no threshold; the live-work FPS is proven on a real call, not sim.
AC-CANVAS-04 tile-ACK <=500ms budget: the named constant is the build budget; the real p100 is a pinned measurement.
Camera↔screen mutual-exclusion + no-black-frame on swap needs a real Output-Media promote/demote cycle to confirm neither stream drops (AC-CANVAS-14).

title: Failure honesty: rejoin-once + honest gap + mark-lost + voice→chat + rate limiter
intent: Every failure mode has an honest, non-silent path — Proxy is never both broken AND pretending (spec §3.7). Bot drop → auto-rejoin exactly once, then an honest terminal stop; on rejoin, state the gap plainly — the announced interval equals the real [dropped,rejoined] window, never fabricated/padded/shrunk, never presented as continuous (the gap line's chat copy is byte-equal to the spoken line). Un-transcribed audio is marked lost (buffer-through on the external BYOK leg is NOT ours); transcript_segments default pending→comprehended, and on close every still-pending segment is backfilled as a gap, none dropped. Voice-down degrades to chat with a 'voice is down — I'll type' notice (never both mute and silent). Recall's shared workspace request limit is paced by a per-bot outbound queue (limits/MemoryStorage moving-window, not a hand-rolled bucket) that WAITS rather than rejecting, so a burst queues instead of throttling.
definition_of_done: Done = a drop fires exactly one rejoin (never a loop), a rejoin-fail/second-drop is an honest terminal stop, the announced gap equals the real window and is never continuous, still-pending segments backfill as gaps on close, voice-down degrades to chat with parity notice, and a send burst queues (delivered==submitted, dropped_by_throttle==0) via the limits-backed gate. NOT done if rejoin loops unbounded, a gap is fabricated/padded, a segment is silently dropped, voice-down leaves the line dropped, or the limiter rejects/drops a send.
integration_point: services/transport/src/transport/failure.py (RejoinPolicy/GapAnnouncer/SegmentReconciler/VoiceChatDegrade) + transport/outbound.py + transport/limiter.py driven by bot-status signals in the harness
acceptance: WHEN the bot drops THE SYSTEM SHALL auto-rejoin exactly once and, on rejoin, announce the real [dropped,rejoined] gap plainly; WHEN voice is down THE SYSTEM SHALL type the line on chat with a notice; WHEN a send burst arrives THE SYSTEM SHALL queue and pace it via the limits-backed gate, dropping none.
invariants: Law 2 never overstate — the announced gap equals the real window; continuity is never faked
Law 1 grounded — un-transcribed audio marked lost, never silently absent
Never both broken and pretending — at least one channel always delivers (voice→chat degrade)
Rate limiter built on the pinned limits/MemoryStorage moving-window, not a hand-rolled token bucket (AC-FAIL-16)
risks: AC-FAIL-09/11 mark-lost under BYOK: confirm-at-build whether Recall buffers through an AAI hiccup — do NOT add a buffer-through handler that over-promises resilience we don't own; the honest path is mark-lost.

AC-FAIL-18 rate-limiter under 5+ concurrent deliveries is a pinned measurement — the burst-queues-not-throttles behavior needs a real concurrency test (the M8 test proves the queue mechanism; live throughput is M11).
Rejoin-once is bounded to a single attempt for the meeting — verify no path re-arms the budget silently (AC-FAIL-06).

title: Provider seams + in-process carrier + signal-surface completeness + platform matrix
intent: Every external piece sits behind a thin Protocol seam — TransportProvider (Recall), STTProvider (AssemblyAI-via-Recall), TTSProvider (Cartesia), OutputMediaSink — so a provider swap is a migration, not a redesign; callers depend ONLY on the Protocols and the concrete SDK symbol appears solely inside its impl module (spec §3.8). The carrier from transport to the projector/canvas and the Orchestrator is a direct in-process asyncio call — no bus, no broker, no socket, no wire (spec §2). The emitted surface covers all nine §3.10 signals with declared payload shapes, stays disjoint from the client ProxyMessage registry, and the platform matrix (join/hear/speak/tile/screenshare across Meet/Zoom/Teams = 15 cells) runs through the one Recall carrier with zero per-platform code and per-meeting DM reporting. The managed cost floor sits honestly in [$0.75,$0.85] bound by the SAME rate-card constants the elapsed×rate accrual uses (not a passes-by-construction constant), reloading monotonically across a recycle.
definition_of_done: Done = each seam is a runtime-checkable Protocol with a lone concrete impl (swap = migration), the carrier is a pure in-process asyncio fan-out (no bus/wire), all nine signals are present with correct payload shapes and disjoint from assert_registry_closed, the 15-cell platform matrix routes through one Recall carrier with zero per-platform branches, and the cost floor binds the real accrual rate-card and reloads monotonically. NOT done if a caller depends on a concrete provider type, a raw client/SDK leaks outside its impl module, a signal enters the client registry, or the floor is a constant sum not bound to accrual.
integration_point: services/transport/src/transport/seams.py (Protocols) + transport/carrier.py (SignalCarrier) + transport/recall.py (sole TransportProvider impl) + transport/surface.py (completeness/matrix) + transport/signals.py (the nine-signal surface)
acceptance: WHEN any provider is swapped THE SYSTEM SHALL require only a new impl behind the Protocol seam (no caller change); the emitted surface SHALL cover all nine §3.10 signals disjoint from the client registry, route the 15-cell platform matrix through one Recall carrier with zero per-platform code, and bind the managed cost floor to the same rate-card the accrual uses.
invariants: In-process carrier — no bus/broker/socket/wire between transport and consumers (spec §2, AC-SEAM-06/07)
Provider independence — callers depend only on Protocols; concrete SDK symbol lives only in its impl module (AC-SEAM-01/08)
Registry disjointness — the nine signals are internal, never client ProxyMessage types (AC-SEAM-12, CANONICAL §11.8)
Cost honesty — floor binds the real accrual rate-card, not a constant sum (AC-SEAM-22); accrual reloads monotonically across recycle (AC-SEAM-15)
risks: AC-SEAM-16/17/19 platform matrix (15 cells across Meet/Zoom/Teams) is STATED not discovered at demo — the real cross-platform join/hear/speak/tile/screenshare is a live-integration claim; the offline test proves the one-carrier/zero-per-platform-code structure only.

The cost floor must bind the SAME config/defaults.toml [transport] rate-card constants the accrual multiplies (AC-SEAM-22) — a divergent hard-coded floor would pass by construction while the real accrual drifts.
fakes.py is test/spike-only scaffolding (M0/M4) — verify no live path depends on FakeTTS/FakeOutputMediaSink; the V0 managed stack is Recall+AssemblyAI+Cartesia (AC-SEAM-05).

title: Delivery verbs + cross-cutting guards (never-throw, naming, secrets, seam, SLO homing) + cost accrual
intent: The three delivery verbs — speak · send_chat · show_screen — are the SOLE delivery authority: every channel emission flows through one of them, and each returns a typed result and NEVER throws (the agentkit never-throw boundary). This node also carries the layer's cross-cutting guard facts and the managed cost accrual: every user-visible transport string (consent notice, ack line, gap line, voice-down notice) carries no internal component name (naming lint over user_visible_strings); no secret is hard-coded; every external Recall/AssemblyAI/Cartesia round-trip flows through the one libs.http.call_external seam with no raw client anywhere in services/transport; the §12.8-pinned latency SLOs stay single-homed in [latency_slo] and the [transport] tunables never redeclare a §12.8 number; there is no screen-ingestion path (the canvas is outbound-only). The rate card lives once in config/defaults.toml and both the floor check and the elapsed×rate accrual read the same constants.
definition_of_done: Done = the three verbs are the only channel emitters and each returns a typed error instead of throwing, no user-visible string leaks an internal name, no secret is hard-coded, every external call routes through call_external (static scan finds no raw client), the §12.8 SLO numbers stay single-homed (no [transport] redeclare), no screen-ingestion path exists, and the cost accrual is a real elapsed×rate computation off the single rate card. NOT done if a channel emission bypasses the verbs, a verb throws, an internal name/secret leaks, a raw provider client appears, or a §12.8 number is duplicated in [transport].
integration_point: services/transport/src/transport/delivery.py (the three delivery verbs + guard facts) + transport/external.py (call_external seam type) + transport/cost.py (rate card + accrual) + transport/config.py (tunables), all wired at meeting_runtime startup
acceptance: WHEN any channel output is delivered THE SYSTEM SHALL emit it only through speak/send_chat/show_screen, each returning a typed result and never throwing; every external call SHALL route through libs.http.call_external, every user-visible string SHALL carry no internal name, and the managed cost SHALL accrue as elapsed×rate off the single rate card.
invariants: Tool handlers never throw — every delivery verb returns errors, never raises (libs.agentkit.tools never-throw boundary, AC-XCUT-11)
Naming — no user-visible transport string contains an internal component name (lint.naming, AC-XCUT-01)
Secrets — no secret hard-coded; check-secret-bindings at startup (AC-XCUT-02)
External calls — every round-trip via the single libs.http.call_external seam; no raw client in services/transport (AC-XCUT-03)
SLO single-homing — §12.8 latency numbers live only in [latency_slo]; [transport] never redeclares one (AC-XCUT-09); no screen-ingestion path (AC-XCUT-10)
risks: AC-XCUT-03 'all external calls through libs.http seam' is a static-scan claim over services/transport — verify no raw Recall/AssemblyAI/Cartesia SDK import sneaks into an impl module bypassing the injected call_external.

AC-XCUT-09 §12.8 SLO single-homing: the [transport] block must carry ONLY numbers not pinned by §12.8 (chunk size, buffer bound, barge-in budget) — a duplicated latency number would create a second source of truth.
The cost accrual is an offline computation; the real $0.75-0.85/hr envelope is validated against actual Recall+AAI+Cartesia spend at M11, not the unit test.
